checklist: worklet.mjs (Chromium, the AudioWorklet path pi-audio takes in a browser): the tarball's index.js imported into an AudioWorkletGlobalScope (no fetch, no importScripts there) instantiates the wasm synchronously from a WebAssembly.Module and from its bytes, inside an OfflineAudioContext at 16000 and 48000 Hz; mic and reference arrive as 128-sample render quanta; a synthetic far end with an 80 ms, -6 dB echo through a four-tap room gives ERLE >= 20 dB, AEC3's own erleDb >= 10 and delayMs within 12 ms of 80; double talk with noise suppression keeps the near end (projection gain >= 0.5, correlation >= 0.6 at latencySamples) with the echo still >= 15 dB down before it; the output is bit-identical to the same cancellation on the page's main thread and from bytes, and latencySamples is 288/384 (16 kHz) and 910/1198 (48 kHz, without/with noise suppression); NaN and ±Infinity in mic and reference (64 + 10 + 2 samples in the 80 ms echo scene, #744) reach the processor through Web Audio and give no non-finite output, stats().nonFiniteSamples equal to 76 and ERLE >= 20 dB after them

lib/node.mjs (ci, Node, the path pi-audio takes with node-web-audio-api): the exports index.d.ts names; the wasm imports only the five functions index.js provides, and index.js has no fetch, importScripts, await, require or import(); synchronous instantiation from a Module, an ArrayBuffer and a Uint8Array; bad options and a destroyed canceller throw; 1000 create/destroy cycles on one instance without wasm memory growth; at both rates: the measured lag of cancel() is exactly latencySamples with and without noise suppression, and the output is bit-identical for chunks of 128, 333, 480 and the whole signal and in place; ERLE >= 20 dB and AEC3's erleDb >= 10 on an 80 ms echo, at >= 3x realtime; delayMs within 12 ms for echoes at 40, 80, 160 and 300 ms, each with ERLE >= 20 dB; double talk keeps the near end (gain >= 0.5, correlation >= 0.6) with and without noise suppression, the echo >= 15 dB down before and after; the VAD flags <= 5% of cancelled echo-only frames and >= 50% of near-end frames; a reference queued ahead past a second is dropped and counted, a missing one is counted; NaN and ±Infinity in mic and reference (64 + 10 + 2 samples in the 80 ms echo scene, #744), with and without noise suppression, give no non-finite output, stats().nonFiniteSamples equal to 76, ERLE >= 20 dB before and after them, and cancel() leaves the caller's arrays unchanged; an all-NaN reference gives the same output as a silent one, and in-place cancel(mic, ref, mic) with non-finite mic samples the same as out of place
